additional_concerns: The definition checks below do not validate the complete relief rules. Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preserved legacy processing into substantive relief exclusion. The circular expressly preserves processing; whether that also defeats relief requires clarification, including treatment after subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question and scope rather than deciding their eligibility. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa answers only substantive qualification. These narrower answers cannot establish actual relief for legacy applications.

The explicit commencement date supports the date threshold, but does not establish a universal assessment-event or implementation-date test. The opening reference to immediate effect should be reconciled with the implementation paragraph before resolving disputed temporal cases.

The relevant SFC FAQs and any authoritative clarification of legacy processing are missing for resolving actual relief and temporal ambiguities. The supplied missing dependency IDs have no identified resource mapping; neither can safely be assigned to a particular authority. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements are also needed to determine concrete home-compliance facts, although they are unnecessary to verify these definition claims.

No separate home-supervision condition is explicit in item (ii). Importing item (i)'s supervision condition would require justification. Relief also does not establish notification compliance, filing compliance or exemption from post-vetting.
